## kb_to_source

- Sentence-by-sentence read of the 27 documents homing this task's four extended policies and their base clauses. Every obligation, eligibility, calculation and order traces to a structured source, with one exception:
  - **damage_protection_schedule_65563e6b, "Points of judgement", second item:** "*Which classes carry a deductible?* Only Ridgeline Rental Aerial and Lifting (250.00) and Ridgeline Rental Earthmoving and Compact Equipment (500.00); every other class shows 0.00." Under rental_ext_damage_deductible, any protected agreement with accidental damage and a repair cost above zero owes a deductible, and the repair-size tiers produce a non-zero deductible in every class ("when the repair cost is below 1,500.00 dollars, the deductible is 25 percent of the repair cost"; "≥ 10,000.00 … the class deductible plus 2 percent of the repair cost above 10,000.00"). The visible corpus itself shows the conflict: repair_size_deductible_f7e9ea3c "Ridgeline Rental Floor and Surface Care | 800.00 | 25 percent of 800.00, that is 200.00". The answer "Only … carry a deductible" is a claim about which agreements owe a deductible that no source sentence makes (the source's class figure is 0.00, not "carries no deductible"), and for the four 0.00 classes it contradicts the extended rule. The trailing "every other class shows 0.00" permits a figure-only reading, but the question as worded is about owing, and nothing visible says which document prevails.
- Cross-problem operational guidance: none (the adjustment hub names only `accept_damage_adjustment_c3a91d5f`; the fee documents say nothing of the dispute or the adjustment).
- Opening world state written in as policy fact: none (no document states that any agreement lacks a deductible, accessory or refuelling line; all examples are marked hypothetical).
- Glosses accepted as entailed: missing_accessory_charge "An accessory is a blade, bit, hose, pad or similar item rented with the unit" (descriptive, no consequence); damage_protection_schedule term definitions "Coverage limit per incident" / "Deductible per incident" (product-figure definitions consistent with the baselines).

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED** — one finding.

- B1 (severity: moderate; untriggered in this task's world — the loader is Earthmoving with a 15840.00 repair).
  - Symptom: the corpus states that only two equipment classes carry a damage deductible, while the in-force deductible rule makes one owed in every class with protection and accidental damage.
  - Root cause: a derived "point of judgement" on the product-figure document carries the pre-extension reading of the class deductible column as a rule about owing; the extended policy's repair-size tiers make it untrue for Hand and Power Tools, Floor and Surface Care, Lawn and Landscape and Concrete and Masonry.
  - Evidence: damage_protection_schedule_65563e6b quotation above; source rental_ext_damage_deductible `rule` ("On an agreement with damage protection whose return inspection found accidental damage with a repair cost above zero, the renter owes the damage deductible for the incident … when the repair cost is below 1,500.00 dollars, the deductible is 25 percent of the repair cost"); factor `repair_size_method` ladder; visible counter-statement in repair_size_deductible_f7e9ea3c worked figures.
  - Affected document and location: damage_protection_schedule_65563e6b, section "Points of judgement", item 2.
  - Effect on a solver: for a protected agreement in one of the four 0.00 classes with accidental damage, the visible materials give two answers (no deductible vs. 25 % of a sub-1500.00 repair or 2 % above 10000.00), so the deductible line, and through the protected repair cost the adjustment, is not uniquely entailed in that branch.
- Everything else in scope: PASS (baselines, all 19 factor ladders with every tier, assembly orders, windows, rounding, retired clauses and the in-force clauses beside them, tool contracts).
- First revision; no previous revision.

## dependency_form

- The three prerequisite sentences stand verbatim in the blocked hub (damage_adjustment_acceptance_77e18897) in state form; none is restated as an action or names a performer or tool.
- Same-form restatement in the same hub: "Restated in the same terms: the amount of the adjustment waits on the agreement showing the damage deductible line owed for the incident, the missing-accessory charge owed from the return inspection and the refuelling charge owed for its fuel reading at return." It joins the blocked policy's own three sentences in the blocked policy's own document, keeps the state form, and states no order among the depended-on problems and no tool. Not a finding.
- No dependency stated in a second document; no aggregated table/checklist/route; no cross-problem example or FAQ; titles general ("Ridgeline Tool Rental Adjustment of Disputed Damage Repair Charges under Damage Protection" names the request type, not this customer's situation).
- Findability from record words: "damage deductible line", "missing-accessory charge … return inspection", "refuelling charge … fuel reading" are the depended-on documents' own terms; each factor document is reachable from the records (repair_cost, accessories_missing, fuel levels, hour meters, reservation/pickup dates, due-back/return dates, damage protection lines, dispute created_at, the Ridgeline Consumer Credit account's tier, opening date, late fees, purchases and their channel).
- **E1 — KB-EXPLICIT RED: two factor documents point at each other.**
  - on_schedule_return_reduction_d5acee4f, paragraph 3: "The two amounts taken off the excess the renter keeps are subtracted after the renter's share of the excess has been figured, and the excess the renter keeps never goes below zero." The same sentence stands in prompt_dispute_reduction_18e0236f, paragraph 3. The hypothetical heading of on_schedule_return_reduction adds "(… share of the excess kept 1885.50 before this reduction, nothing else taken off)".
  - What it states beyond the source's form: each document's subject is one reduction, yet "the two amounts" tells the reader that a second, unnamed reduction of the excess kept exists, and "nothing else taken off" signals that other subtractions can apply. A reader who found either factor from the records is told to look for the other, so that factor's discovery is handed over rather than derived from the records (the dispute's filing date, the return date). The source carries this as an assembly sentence of the extended `rule` ("The two amounts taken off are subtracted after the renter's share of the excess has been figured, and the excess the renter keeps never goes below zero"); the semantics that must stay visible are the order (subtract after the share is figured) and the floor at zero, not the count of reductions.
  - In this task's blind audit both reductions were in fact found from the records (prompt filing day 4; return on the due-back date), so the hop is correct; this is recorded once here, as the skill requires.
- Non-findings recorded for completeness: worked figures echo across documents (excess 3271.00 in protected_damage_adjustment_amount_90975077 and excess_sharing_rental_history_a442b0c9; 1885.50 from the excess-sharing example reused in on_schedule_return_reduction; priced refuelling 137.40 in contract_fuel_price_e98b078b equal to the full-tank figure of refuelling_pricing_by_shortfall_828d5ae0). They are numerical echoes without words that name or point to another document or factor, so they are not judged a pointer; noted because they line up the illustrations of different factors.

**KB-EXPLICIT RED** (E1).

### B1 — closure check

- The new item 2 is a figure-reading question about the schedule column ("the deductible per incident on this schedule … the schedule figure … is 0.00"); it no longer says which classes owe a deductible. It is now consistent with the baseline (damage_deductible_amount_fe2d307f: "the class deductible … never more than the repair cost") and leaves the repair-size tiers (repair_size_deductible_f7e9ea3c, incl. "Floor and Surface Care | 800.00 | … 200.00") uncontradicted. A search of the corpus for any other statement that a class carries no deductible finds only the source-backed "Agreements without damage protection, and inspections that found no accidental damage, carry no damage deductible" (damage_deductible_amount_fe2d307f).
- Nothing dropped: the removed sentence had no structured source, so its removal takes no atom away. The column definition "Deductible per incident: the amount per incident the renter pays even with damage protection" is unchanged and was accepted in round 1 as a product-figure definition consistent with the baseline.
- **B1 closed.**

### E1 — closure check

- Neither reduction document now refers to a second amount; "two amounts" now occurs only in settlement_6da81e3d (balance and deposit, unrelated). The phrase "nothing else taken off" is gone from on_schedule_return_reduction_d5acee4f ("nothing else" now occurs only in open_agreement_limits_f3d5ad28, a hypothetical about the renter's file).
- The semantics the source requires are kept at the same strength in each document: subtract after the share of the excess has been figured, never below zero, no rounding on the way, rounding only at the end. Equivalence with the source's single sentence: the source floors once after both subtractions; the documents floor after each. Because both amounts are non-negative, max(0, max(0, s − a) − b) = max(0, s − a − b) for every s, so no permitted result changes. Not a bijection defect.
- The new example 1200.00 is not the output of another factor's worked figures (round 1's 1885.50 echoed excess_sharing_rental_history_a442b0c9); arithmetic checked (1200.00 − 150.00 = 1050.00; − 75.00 = 1125.00; 1200.00).
- **E1 closed.**
